entries.title: Structure can follow your mouse, as an experiment
entries.body: Structure has a third view, Hover, beside Fisheye and Expanded. In its two-column view, rest your mouse on a row in either column for a moment and the article scrolls to that passage without a click; a click still jumps as before. It works with a mouse only, and it is behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Chat is asked to introduce what it names
entries.body: When an answer in Chat, or in Learn's Recall and Explore conversations, names a person, a study, a work or a term, the AI is asked to say in a few words who or what it is and why it matters here. Chat's list of conversations also says beneath each title where it started: Investigate, Claims, Bibliography, Glossary or Ideas.

entries.title: Marginalia gives the chat card more room
entries.body: When Marginalia shows its notes beside the article and no other panel is open, the article can shift further left on narrower windows, so the chat card and the notes column can be wider. The article's own width does not change, and nothing jumps as you resize the window.

entries.title: A contents list at the start folds away
entries.body: When an article opens with its own table of contents but no heading above it, the app can recognise it by its links to the article's later sections and fold it into a Contents line you can open. Lists that follow a label such as Key points stay visible.

entries.title: More web pages show their publication date
entries.body: When you add a web page that prints its date under the title, or carries the day in its address, but does not record a date in its hidden page details, the app reads that date and shows it above the article. Before, no date appeared for such pages.

entries.title: The Help question box grows as you type
entries.body: On the Help page, when you are signed in, the box for asking a question starts two lines tall and grows to fit what you write, with no scroll bar inside it and no handle to drag.

entries.title: arXiv paper titles keep their full wording
entries.body: Some arXiv papers came in with a broken title: two parts run together with no space, or the part before a colon cut off. When you add such a paper, its title is read correctly, in your library, above the article and in the browser tab.

entries.title: Cross-references no longer report a failed import
entries.body: Adding cross-references (links from a claim to the passage behind it) could fail when every link the AI proposed pointed to the same or a neighbouring paragraph; it finishes with none instead. When an extra like this does fail, its card says the article itself is unchanged, rather than suggesting the import failed.
